issues.legal_issue: An assignment of leasehold land and buildings is chargeable as a conveyance under the applicable stamp-duty schedule article.
material_facts: The instrument assigned the transferor’s interests in leased land and a building to an incorporated company.
The instrument was referred for determination of the stamp duty chargeable on it.
issues.conclusion: The applicable article was the conveyance article in the First Schedule to the Indian Stamp Act.
issues.legal_principle: Article 23 of the First Schedule applies to a conveyance as defined by section 2(10) of the Indian Stamp Act.

predicates.stamp_duty_classification_dispute: A dispute concerns the stamp-duty classification of an instrument.
predicates.instrument_assigns_interests_in_leasehol: An instrument transfers interests in leased land and buildings from one person to another.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty classification dispute concerns an instrument transferring interests in leased land and buildings, the instrument is chargeable as a conveyance.

issues.legal_issue: Revenue authorities may not independently investigate the value of property conveyed to determine stamp duty when the instrument states no consideration.
material_facts: The assignment instrument stated that the transfer was for no consideration.
The revenue authority assessed duty using a value derived from outside the instrument.
Section 27 required the parties to state consideration and other relevant facts fully and truly, while failure to comply was punishable under section 64.
The Stamp Act contained no provision empowering revenue authorities to conduct an independent inquiry into the value of the conveyed property for determining duty.
issues.conclusion: The revenue authority was not empowered to make an independent inquiry into the value of the conveyed property to determine stamp duty.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 23 of the First Schedule to the Indian Stamp Act, the relevant consideration is that set forth in the instrument. Section 27 requires full and truthful disclosure in the instrument, and section 64 provides punishment for failure to comply; neither authorizes an independent valuation inquiry by revenue authorities. The Court approved Ramen Chetty v. Mohomed Ghouse, Sakharam Shankar v. Ramchandra Babu Mohire, Muhammad Muzaffar Ali, In re, Sri Sitaram Ramalia v. State of Bihar, and Bharpet Mohammad Hussain Sahib v. District Registrar, Kurnool.

predicates.stamp_duty_valuation_dispute: A dispute concerns the determination of stamp duty on an instrument conveying property.
predicates.instrument_declares_no_consideration: The instrument states that the conveyance is made for no consideration.
predicates.authority_uses_external_valuation: A revenue authority relies on a valuation independent of the instrument to determine the duty.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty valuation dispute involves an instrument declaring no consideration and an authority relying on an external valuation, the authority cannot independently inquire into the conveyed value.

issues.legal_issue: A reference to earlier agreements in an assignment instrument does not incorporate their terms unless the instrument shows that the parties intended to incorporate them.
material_facts: The assignment instrument’s preamble referred to earlier grants of rights to occupy flats, offices, and shops.
The instrument did not state that the terms and conditions of those earlier agreements formed part of the assignment.
Most of the earlier agreements were not before the Court.
issues.conclusion: The earlier agreements were not incorporated into the assignment instrument merely because it referred to the earlier transactions.
issues.legal_principle: Terms of an agreement become incorporated into another document only when that document shows that the parties intended to incorporate them; a mere reference to earlier transactions does not suffice.

predicates.stamp_duty_document_dispute: A dispute concerns the treatment of an instrument for stamp-duty purposes.
predicates.document_refers_to_earlier_agreements: An instrument mentions agreements made before it was executed.
predicates.document_shows_intent_to_incorporate_the: The instrument shows that its parties intended the earlier agreements’ terms to form part of it.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty document dispute involves an instrument that mentions earlier agreements but does not show an intention to incorporate their terms, those terms are not incorporated.

issues.legal_issue: Payments made under earlier arrangements are not consideration for a later assignment when the beneficiaries had already acquired independent rights that did not flow from that assignment.
material_facts: Occupiers had acquired rights in flats, offices, or shops under earlier arrangements before the assignment was executed.
Those rights were independent of, and did not derive from, the later assignment.
The revenue authority treated amounts paid under the earlier arrangements as consideration for the later assignment.
issues.conclusion: There was no basis to treat the amounts paid under the earlier arrangements as consideration for the assignment.
issues.legal_principle: Amounts paid under prior arrangements do not constitute consideration for a later assignment where the rights obtained under those arrangements were independently acquired before the assignment and did not flow from it.

predicates.stamp_duty_consideration_dispute: A dispute concerns the consideration relevant to stamp duty on an assignment.
predicates.prior_beneficiaries_acquired_rights_befo: Beneficiaries obtained rights under earlier arrangements before the later assignment was executed.
predicates.prior_rights_did_not_flow_from_assignmen: The beneficiaries’ earlier rights arose independently and did not derive from the later assignment.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty consideration dispute concerns a later assignment and beneficiaries had already acquired independent rights that did not flow from it, payments made under the earlier arrangements are not consideration for that assignment.

issues.legal_issue: An assignment instrument that does not purport to be a gift is not chargeable as a gift merely because it states that no consideration is given.
material_facts: The assignment instrument transferred interests in land and a building and stated that no consideration was given.
The instrument did not purport to be a gift.
The suggested gift classification was not elaborated, and the gift article prescribed duty on the same valuation basis as a conveyance.
issues.conclusion: The assignment was not to be treated as a gift; the gift contention had no merit.
issues.legal_principle: Article 33 of the First Schedule to the Indian Stamp Act applies to a gift, but the instrument in this case did not purport to be one. In any event, Article 33 assessed duty on the same basis as a conveyance, by reference to the value set forth in the instrument.

predicates.stamp_duty_classification_dispute: A dispute concerns the stamp-duty classification of an instrument.
predicates.instrument_does_not_purport_to_be_a_gift: The instrument does not characterize or present the transfer as a gift.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty classification dispute concerns an instrument that does not purport to be a gift, the instrument is not chargeable as a gift.
